subject: Architecture
title: Drone-Built Bridges: Robots Over the Gap
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Drone-Built Bridges: Robots Over the Gap.

hook.text: In 2015, drones wove a rope bridge across a canyon in Switzerland. No human touched the cables.

buildup.text: ETH Zurich programmed drones to fly tensile ropes between anchor points, weaving a walkable span.

discovery.text: Drone construction eliminates scaffolding, reduces worker risk, and reaches terrain no crane can.

twist.text: Military engineers now use drones to deploy emergency bridges in disaster zones within hours.

climax.text: Researchers are testing drones that 3D-print concrete mid-flight, building structure as they move.

punchline.text: The next great bridge might be built without a single worker on site.

quiz.question: What did ETH Zurich's drones build in Switzerland?
options: A concrete arch bridge over a river
A rope bridge woven across a canyon
A steel truss bridge in a remote valley
